# chezmoi-dotfiles

This machine's `$HOME` is managed by a **chezmoi** (configs) + **ansible** (system
deps) dotfiles repo. This skill is the agent-facing map: how to drive it, and what
custom tooling exists that you wouldn't otherwise know about. It is rendered per-host
— the "What's enabled on THIS machine" section reflects what the user actually
selected at init.

## Orientation (read this first)

- **Repo root**: `chezmoi source-path` (no args) prints the source dir. Work there
  to edit: `cd "$(chezmoi source-path)"`.
- **Source path of one file**: `chezmoi source-path ~/.config/foo/bar` → the
  managed source file for that target.
- **`docs/**` is NOT deployed to `$HOME`** (it's chezmoi-ignored). Read detail via
  `"$(chezmoi source-path)/docs/..."`. A *subset* is deployed to `~/.config/docs/`
  (e.g. keybindings, cli-tools) for runtime helpers.
- **Read the contract before editing**: `"$(chezmoi source-path)/CLAUDE.md"` holds
  Hard invariants and cross-file maintenance rules. Honor them.
- This host: profile `macos_intel`, OS `darwin`/`amd64`, primary shell `zsh`.

## chezmoi essentials

```bash
chezmoi diff                 # preview changes (also: just chezmoi-diff)
chezmoi apply                # deploy + run scripts (also: cas, or just chezmoi-apply)
chezmoi status               # modified/added/removed targets
chezmoi edit ~/.zshrc        # edit the SOURCE of a target
chezmoi add  ~/.config/x     # start managing an existing file
chezmoi re-add               # pull live edits back into source
chezmoi managed | grep foo   # is X managed?
chezmoi cat ~/.config/x      # render a target without applying
chezmoi data | jq            # the template data (ground truth for the toggles below)
```

- **`cas`** = `chezmoi apply` + reload hint; **`cau`** = update from remote then apply
  (defined in `dot_config/shell/99_chezmoi_reload.sh`).
- **`dotcfg`** = reconfigure the init prompts on an already-set-up machine
  (`dotcfg` for the TUI, `dotcfg --set installLlmTools=true --yes` for one toggle,
  `dotcfg --dry-run` to preview). Shell twin: `czcfg`.
- **Never `chezmoi add` a `modify_`/`create_` target** — it overwrites the script.
- Full command cheat-sheet: `docs/this_repo/cheatsheet.md`. Install-vs-upgrade is
  split: `chezmoi apply`/ansible is **install-only**; upgrades go through
  `just upgrade-*`.

## What's enabled on THIS machine

(Rendered from this host's selections. For live truth: `chezmoi data | jq`.)
- **Coding agents** — Claude Code, OpenCode, Cursor, Codex, Gemini, Copilot (configs + CLIs). See `docs/tools/agent-overlays.md`, `docs/tools/agent-skills.md`.
- **Python uv tools** — mlflow, marimo, jupyter, etc. (powers the `mlf` CLI). See `docs/this_repo/uv-bootstrap.md`.
- **Extra runtimes** — rust, bun, ruby via mise (+ cargo/gem tools). Node is always present.
- **LLM tools** — Ollama / LiteLLM / local models.
- **JS CLI tools** — standalone npm CLIs (e.g. readability-cli).
- **.NET tools** — .NET SDK (mise) + dotnet global tools.
- **IaC** — Azure CLI, Terraform, OpenTofu.
- **Media** — ffmpeg, ImageMagick, exiftool, libvips.
- **Media control** — nowplaying-cli + switchaudio-osx (macOS) / playerctl (Linux); unlocks full `sysplay`/`sysnow` (built-in `sysvol`/`sysmute` work regardless).
- **Networking** — nmap, mtr, httpie, gping, trippy.
- **Tunnels** — ngrok, cloudflared.
- **Vim mode** — shell modal editing + tmux vim nav (NOT Neovim/editors — those are always vim).

## Custom in-house CLIs (always deployed to `~/.dotfiles/bin`, on PATH)

Each works from any cwd. Run with `--help`, or read `docs/tools/<name>.md`. Full list: `ls "$(chezmoi source-path)/dot_dotfiles/bin/"`.

- **`fleet`** — cross-host ops over your machines: `fleet chezmoi apply`, `fleet hosts`, `fleet tmux`, `fleet info`, `fleet pueue`, `fleet exec`. See `docs/this_repo/fleet-apply.md`, `docs/tools/fleet-exec.md`, `docs/tools/fleet-hosts.md`.
- **`mlf`** — MLflow umbrella CLI + TUI dashboard (needs Python uv tools). Picker twin: `tv mlflow`.
- **`pqsum`** — pueue queue summary (text / AI / JSON). See `docs/tools/pueue.md`.
- **`x`** — clipboard/file copy-paste-open with cross-platform fallbacks.
- **`mi-router`** / **`reyee`** / **`sms`** — read-only router CLIs (Xiaomi MiWiFi / Ruijie Reyee / Huawei HiLink SMS). See `docs/tools/{mi-router,reyee,sms}.md`.
- **`ping-monitor`** — record ping over time, flag latency spikes. See `docs/tools/ping-monitor.md`.
- **`dotcfg`** — reconfigure dotfiles prompts (above).
- **`sesh-preview`** — preview helper for the sesh picker.

## Television (`tv`) — fuzzy pickers with custom channels

There are ~40 **custom** channels (system state, fleet, services, infra, agents…)
that you won't discover otherwise. Browse them:

```bash
tv                      # default picker
tv list-channels        # list everything available
tv <channel>            # open one, e.g. tv fleet-hosts | tv mlflow | tv pueue
ls "$(chezmoi source-path)/dot_config/television/cable/"   # the channel definitions
```

Handy ones: `fleet-hosts`, `mlflow`, `pueue`, `ports`, `kill-process`, `services`,
`sessions`, `keybindings`, `aliases`, `git-ops`, `mac-apps`/`linux-apps`. Full
reference: `docs/tools/tv.md`.

## Keybindings & keymaps

- **`bindings`** (shell function) or **`tv keybindings`** — interactive reference.
- **tmux**: `prefix + Space` (or `prefix + e`) opens the action menu;
  `prefix + T` = sesh picker, `prefix + U` = tools. Deep ref: `docs/tools/tmux/keybindings.md`.
- **shell ZLE widgets**: `Alt+S` sesh sessions, `Alt+T` tools, `Ctrl+R` history (atuin).
- Master reference: `docs/shells/keybindings.md` (also deployed to `~/.config/docs/shells/keybindings.md`).

## Aliases & functions

`alias` to list shell aliases, or `tv aliases`. Catalog: `docs/shells/aliases.md`.
Helpers worth knowing: `chezmoi-cd` (jump to source), `run-for` (time-box a command),
`bindings` (above). App control: `applaunch`/`appquit`/`apprestart`/… (cross-platform).
System audio (cross-platform, built-in): `sysvol`/`sysmute` (+ `sysplay`/`sysnow` with `installMediaControl`); remote mute via `fleet exec --login -- sysmute on`.

## just recipes (run from the source dir)

```bash
cd "$(chezmoi source-path)" && just --list
```

Categories: `chezmoi-*`, `ansible-*`, `upgrade-*` (brew/mise/uv/npm/cargo/…),
`fleet`/`fleet-*`, `gen-prompts` (regenerate prompt scaffolding), `check`/`lint`,
`docker-*`. See `docs/this_repo/cheatsheet.md`.

## Editing rules (don't skip)

Before changing anything under the repo, read `CLAUDE.md` Hard invariants and the
"Cross-file maintenance rules" table — many surfaces have mandatory mirror updates
in the same commit (docs, completions, tool-managers index, this very skill, …).

 `./docs/neovim/copy-reference.md`

```text
1	# Copy Cursor-style file references (`@file:line`)
2	
3	Four Neovim keymaps that copy a **Cursor / Claude Code style file reference** —
4	`@path`, `@path:12`, or `@path:12-40` — to the system clipboard, built from the
5	current buffer plus the cursor line (normal mode), the visual selection
6	(visual mode), or — in a file explorer — the node under the cursor. The `@` triggers the agent's file-mention and the `:line[-line]`
7	points it at exact code, so you paste an exact pointer instead of retyping paths
8	and line numbers by hand.
9	
10	All four live in `lua/config/keymaps.lua` under a `<leader>y` ("copy ref")
11	which-key group. Press `<leader>y` (Space then `y`) to see them.
12	
13	## Keymaps
14	
15	`<leader>` = Space. Every key works in **normal** and **visual** mode.
16	
17	| Keymap | Path flavor | Normal mode (cursor line) | Visual mode (selection) |
18	|--------|-------------|---------------------------|-------------------------|
19	| `<leader>yr` | project-relative | `@rel/path:12` | `@rel/path:12-40` |
20	| `<leader>ya` | machine-absolute | `@/abs/path:12` | `@/abs/path:12-40` |
21	| `<leader>yf` | project-relative | `@rel/path` (no line) | `@rel/path` (no line) |
22	| `<leader>yF` | machine-absolute | `@/abs/path` (no line) | `@/abs/path` (no line) |
23	
24	Mnemonic: `r`elative / `a`bsolute carry the line; `f`ile-only (capital `F` =
25	absolute) is the bare path. Together the four cover all three reference shapes:
26	
27	- `@file` → `<leader>yf`
28	- `@file:line` → `<leader>yr` in normal mode
29	- `@file:line1-line2` → `<leader>yr` in visual mode
30	
31	A single-line visual selection collapses `:12-12` → `:12`. After copying in
32	visual mode the mapping leaves visual mode and shows a `Copied @…` toast.
33	
34	## Path flavors
35	
36	- **Relative** (`yr` / `yf`) is resolved against the **git root**
37	  (`LazyVim.root.git()` — the same root used by [Floating TUI](floating-tui.md)).
38	  A file outside the git root falls back to a `~` / cwd-relative path.
39	- **Absolute** (`ya` / `yF`) is the full machine path (`expand("%:p")`), with no
40	  symlink resolution.
41	
42	Relative is usually what you want for Claude Code (it operates inside the
43	project); absolute is for files outside the repo, or when a tool needs the full
44	path.
45	
46	## File explorers (neo-tree / snacks)
47	
48	Trigger a keymap while focused in a **file-explorer** buffer and the reference
49	points at the **node under the cursor** instead (no line number) — e.g.
50	`<leader>yf` on a tree entry copies `@rel/path/to/that/file`. This mirrors
51	neo-tree's own `Y` (copy path).
52	
53	- **neo-tree** is supported today (resolves the node via neo-tree's manager API).
54	- **snacks explorer** — LazyVim's neo-tree successor — is handled best-effort, so
55	  the keymaps keep working after that migration.
56	- Any other special buffer (terminal, help, quickfix, an unknown explorer, an
57	  unnamed buffer) is safely rejected with a `copy-ref: no file under cursor here`
58	  warning — never a bogus `@neo-tree filesystem [1]`.
59	
60	## Implementation notes
61	
62	The feature is a small `copy_ref_target()` + `copy_reference()` helper pair plus
63	four `vim.keymap.set({ "n", "x" }, …)` calls in `lua/config/keymaps.lua`. It
64	reuses, with no new dependencies:
65	
66	- `LazyVim.root.git()` — git-root detection.
67	- `vim.fs.relpath(root, abspath)` — built-in relative-path computation.
68	- `vim.fn.setreg("+", ref)` — respects the OSC 52 clipboard provider configured
69	  in `lua/config/options.lua`, so it copies into your local terminal clipboard
70	  even over SSH. Do **not** shell out to `pbcopy` — that bypasses OSC 52. See
71	  [Clipboard](../tools/clipboard.md).
72	- Visual range via `vim.fn.line(".")` / `vim.fn.line("v")` — the same pattern the
73	  gitsigns stage-selection maps use.
74	
75	Buffer resolution lives in a `copy_ref_target()` helper: real file buffers
76	(empty `buftype`) yield the file plus line context; known explorers yield the
77	node under the cursor; everything else returns `nil` and the caller warns.
78	Explorer lookups are `pcall`-wrapped so a changed or absent API degrades to that
79	warning instead of crashing or emitting a garbage path. A deleted cwd is likewise
80	guarded with `pcall` (avoids the Neovim 0.12 `vim.fs.find` ENOENT trap) and falls
81	back to a relative path.
82	
83	## Why `<leader>y`
84	
85	`<leader>y` was an unused prefix. The AI keymaps under `<leader>a` are already
86	crowded — avante and claudecode both bind many `<leader>a…` keys and even
87	collide with each other — so a fresh `y` ("yank / copy") group keeps these
88	reference-copy actions clear of that contention and easy to find in which-key.
89	
90	To change or extend the set, edit the `copy_reference` helper and the
91	`vim.keymap.set` block in `lua/config/keymaps.lua`.
92
```
</details></tool-use>

# chezmoi-dotfiles

This machine's `$HOME` is managed by a **chezmoi** (configs) + **ansible** (system
deps) dotfiles repo. This skill is the agent-facing map: how to drive it, and what
custom tooling exists that you wouldn't otherwise know about. It is rendered per-host
— the "What's enabled on THIS machine" section reflects what the user actually
selected at init.

## Orientation (read this first)

- **Repo root**: `chezmoi source-path` (no args) prints the source dir. Work there
  to edit: `cd "$(chezmoi source-path)"`.
- **Source path of one file**: `chezmoi source-path ~/.config/foo/bar` → the
  managed source file for that target.
- **`docs/**` is NOT deployed to `$HOME`** (it's chezmoi-ignored). Read detail via
  `"$(chezmoi source-path)/docs/..."`. A *subset* is deployed to `~/.config/docs/`
  (e.g. keybindings, cli-tools) for runtime helpers.
- **Read the contract before editing**: `"$(chezmoi source-path)/CLAUDE.md"` holds
  Hard invariants and cross-file maintenance rules. Honor them.
- This host: profile `macos_intel`, OS `darwin`/`amd64`, primary shell `zsh`.

## chezmoi essentials

```bash
chezmoi diff                 # preview changes (also: just chezmoi-diff)
chezmoi apply                # deploy + run scripts (also: cas, or just chezmoi-apply)
chezmoi status               # modified/added/removed targets
chezmoi edit ~/.zshrc        # edit the SOURCE of a target
chezmoi add  ~/.config/x     # start managing an existing file
chezmoi re-add               # pull live edits back into source
chezmoi managed | grep foo   # is X managed?
chezmoi cat ~/.config/x      # render a target without applying
chezmoi data | jq            # the template data (ground truth for the toggles below)
```

- **`cas`** = `chezmoi apply` + reload hint; **`cau`** = update from remote then apply
  (defined in `dot_config/shell/99_chezmoi_reload.sh`).
- **`dotcfg`** = reconfigure the init prompts on an already-set-up machine
  (`dotcfg` for the TUI, `dotcfg --set installLlmTools=true --yes` for one toggle,
  `dotcfg --dry-run` to preview). Shell twin: `czcfg`.
- **Never `chezmoi add` a `modify_`/`create_` target** — it overwrites the script.
- Full command cheat-sheet: `docs/this_repo/cheatsheet.md`. Install-vs-upgrade is
  split: `chezmoi apply`/ansible is **install-only**; upgrades go through
  `just upgrade-*`.

## What's enabled on THIS machine

(Rendered from this host's selections. For live truth: `chezmoi data | jq`.)
- **Coding agents** — Claude Code, OpenCode, Cursor, Codex, Gemini, Copilot (configs + CLIs). See `docs/tools/agent-overlays.md`, `docs/tools/agent-skills.md`.
- **Python uv tools** — mlflow, marimo, jupyter, etc. (powers the `mlf` CLI). See `docs/this_repo/uv-bootstrap.md`.
- **Extra runtimes** — rust, bun, ruby via mise (+ cargo/gem tools). Node is always present.
- **LLM tools** — Ollama / LiteLLM / local models.
- **JS CLI tools** — standalone npm CLIs (e.g. readability-cli).
- **.NET tools** — .NET SDK (mise) + dotnet global tools.
- **IaC** — Azure CLI, Terraform, OpenTofu.
- **Media** — ffmpeg, ImageMagick, exiftool, libvips.
- **Media control** — nowplaying-cli + switchaudio-osx (macOS) / playerctl (Linux); unlocks full `sysplay`/`sysnow` (built-in `sysvol`/`sysmute` work regardless).
- **Networking** — nmap, mtr, httpie, gping, trippy.
- **Tunnels** — ngrok, cloudflared.
- **Vim mode** — shell modal editing + tmux vim nav (NOT Neovim/editors — those are always vim).

## Custom in-house CLIs (always deployed to `~/.dotfiles/bin`, on PATH)

Each works from any cwd. Run with `--help`, or read `docs/tools/<name>.md`. Full list: `ls "$(chezmoi source-path)/dot_dotfiles/bin/"`.

- **`fleet`** — cross-host ops over your machines: `fleet chezmoi apply`, `fleet hosts`, `fleet tmux`, `fleet info`, `fleet pueue`, `fleet exec`. See `docs/this_repo/fleet-apply.md`, `docs/tools/fleet-exec.md`, `docs/tools/fleet-hosts.md`.
- **`mlf`** — MLflow umbrella CLI + TUI dashboard (needs Python uv tools). Picker twin: `tv mlflow`.
- **`pqsum`** — pueue queue summary (text / AI / JSON). See `docs/tools/pueue.md`.
- **`x`** — clipboard/file copy-paste-open with cross-platform fallbacks.
- **`mi-router`** / **`reyee`** / **`sms`** — read-only router CLIs (Xiaomi MiWiFi / Ruijie Reyee / Huawei HiLink SMS). See `docs/tools/{mi-router,reyee,sms}.md`.
- **`ping-monitor`** — record ping over time, flag latency spikes. See `docs/tools/ping-monitor.md`.
- **`dotcfg`** — reconfigure dotfiles prompts (above).
- **`sesh-preview`** — preview helper for the sesh picker.

## Television (`tv`) — fuzzy pickers with custom channels

There are ~40 **custom** channels (system state, fleet, services, infra, agents…)
that you won't discover otherwise. Browse them:

```bash
tv                      # default picker
tv list-channels        # list everything available
tv <channel>            # open one, e.g. tv fleet-hosts | tv mlflow | tv pueue
ls "$(chezmoi source-path)/dot_config/television/cable/"   # the channel definitions
```

Handy ones: `fleet-hosts`, `mlflow`, `pueue`, `ports`, `kill-process`, `services`,
`sessions`, `keybindings`, `aliases`, `git-ops`, `mac-apps`/`linux-apps`. Full
reference: `docs/tools/tv.md`.

## Keybindings & keymaps

- **`bindings`** (shell function) or **`tv keybindings`** — interactive reference.
- **tmux**: `prefix + Space` (or `prefix + e`) opens the action menu;
  `prefix + T` = sesh picker, `prefix + U` = tools. Deep ref: `docs/tools/tmux/keybindings.md`.
- **shell ZLE widgets**: `Alt+S` sesh sessions, `Alt+T` tools, `Ctrl+R` history (atuin).
- Master reference: `docs/shells/keybindings.md` (also deployed to `~/.config/docs/shells/keybindings.md`).

## Aliases & functions

`alias` to list shell aliases, or `tv aliases`. Catalog: `docs/shells/aliases.md`.
Helpers worth knowing: `chezmoi-cd` (jump to source), `run-for` (time-box a command),
`bindings` (above). App control: `applaunch`/`appquit`/`apprestart`/… (cross-platform).
System audio (cross-platform, built-in): `sysvol`/`sysmute` (+ `sysplay`/`sysnow` with `installMediaControl`); remote mute via `fleet exec --login -- sysmute on`.

## just recipes (run from the source dir)

```bash
cd "$(chezmoi source-path)" && just --list
```

Categories: `chezmoi-*`, `ansible-*`, `upgrade-*` (brew/mise/uv/npm/cargo/…),
`fleet`/`fleet-*`, `gen-prompts` (regenerate prompt scaffolding), `check`/`lint`,
`docker-*`. See `docs/this_repo/cheatsheet.md`.

## Editing rules (don't skip)

Before changing anything under the repo, read `CLAUDE.md` Hard invariants and the
"Cross-file maintenance rules" table — many surfaces have mandatory mirror updates
in the same commit (docs, completions, tool-managers index, this very skill, …).

```text
24	local function copy_ref_target()

37	      local mgr = require("neo-tree.sources.manager")
38	      local state = mgr.get_state_for_window(vim.api.nvim_get_current_win())
39	      local node = state and state.tree and state.tree:get_node()
40	      return node and (node.path or node:get_id()) or nil
41	    elseif ft == "snacks_picker_list" then

53	  end

57	local function copy_reference(opts)

59	  if not abspath then

84	      if a > b then
85	        a, b = b, a
86	      end
87	      suffix = (a == b) and (":" .. a) or (":" .. a .. "-" .. b)

90	    end
91	  end
92	  if visual then
93	    vim.api.nvim_feedkeys(vim.keycode("<Esc>"), "n", false) -- leave visual mode
94	  end

97	  vim.fn.setreg("+", ref)
98	  vim.notify("Copied " .. ref, vim.log.levels.INFO)
```

```text
1	# ~/.config/shell/58_abspath.sh
2	# Source: dot_config/shell/58_abspath.sh (managed by chezmoi)
3	#
4	# `abspath` — print absolute path(s), POSIX, sourced by both zsh and bash.
5	#   - no args  -> behaves like `pwd` (LOGICAL cwd, symlinks intact)
6	#   - FILE...  -> one absolute path per line
7	#   -r/--resolve : resolve symlinks to the physical path (requires existence)
8	#   -t/--tilde   : abbreviate a $HOME-rooted result to `~`
9	# Pairs with the `x` clipboard CLI:  abspath FILE | x copy
10	#
11	# stdout is pipe-clean (paths only); usage/errors go to stderr.
12	#
13	# Logical base MUST be the shell's $PWD, not python's os.getcwd() (which is
14	# physical / symlink-resolved) — otherwise no-arg output wouldn't equal `pwd`.
15	
16	_abspath_usage() {
17	    printf '%s\n' \
18	        "Usage: abspath [-r|--resolve] [-t|--tilde] [--] [PATH...]" \
19	        "  (no PATH) print the current directory, like pwd" \
20	        "  PATH...   print each path's absolute form, one per line" \
21	        "  -r        resolve symlinks to the physical path (must exist)" \
22	        "  -t        abbreviate a \$HOME-rooted result to ~" \
23	        "Examples:" \
24	        "  abspath                 # == pwd" \
25	        "  abspath foo.py ../bar   # absolute paths" \
26	        "  abspath -t ~/notes.md   # ~/notes.md" \
27	        "  abspath foo.py | x copy"
28	}
29	
30	abspath() {
31	    _ap_resolve=0
32	    _ap_tilde=0
33	    while [ "$#" -gt 0 ]; do
34	        case "$1" in
35	            -r|--resolve) _ap_resolve=1; shift ;;
36	            -t|--tilde)   _ap_tilde=1;   shift ;;
37	            -h|--help)    _abspath_usage; unset _ap_resolve _ap_tilde; return 0 ;;
38	            --)           shift; break ;;
39	            -*)           printf 'abspath: unknown option: %s\n' "$1" >&2
40	                          _abspath_usage >&2
41	                          unset _ap_resolve _ap_tilde; return 2 ;;
42	            *)            break ;;
43	        esac
44	    done
45	
46	    if ! command -v python3 >/dev/null 2>&1; then
47	        printf 'abspath: python3 required for path normalization\n' >&2
48	        unset _ap_resolve _ap_tilde; return 127
49	    fi
50	
51	    ABSPATH_BASE="$PWD" ABSPATH_RESOLVE="$_ap_resolve" ABSPATH_TILDE="$_ap_tilde" \
52	        python3 - "$@" <<'PY'
53	import os, sys
54	
55	base    = os.environ.get("ABSPATH_BASE") or os.getcwd()
56	resolve = os.environ.get("ABSPATH_RESOLVE") == "1"
57	tilde   = os.environ.get("ABSPATH_TILDE") == "1"
58	home    = os.path.expanduser("~")
59	args    = sys.argv[1:] or ["."]          # no args -> current dir, like pwd
60	rc = 0
61	
62	def abbrev(p):
63	    if not tilde:
64	        return p
65	    if p == home:
66	        return "~"
67	    if p.startswith(home + os.sep):
68	        return "~" + p[len(home):]
69	    return p
70	
71	for a in args:
72	    joined = a if os.path.isabs(a) else os.path.join(base, a)
73	    if resolve:
74	        p = os.path.realpath(joined)     # physical; follows symlinks
75	        if not os.path.exists(p):
76	            sys.stderr.write("abspath: no such file or directory: %s\n" % a)
77	            rc = 1
78	            continue
79	    else:
80	        p = os.path.normpath(joined)     # lexical; keeps symlinks, no existence req.
81	    print(abbrev(p))
82	
83	sys.exit(rc)
84	PY
85	    _ap_rc=$?
86	    unset _ap_resolve _ap_tilde
87	    return "$_ap_rc"
88	}
89
```

44	### Workmux status icon integration spans 6 files
45	
46	Touching the `🤖`/`💬`/`✅` per-tmux-window status mechanism requires keeping these 6 surfaces in sync (full story: [docs/tools/workmux.md](docs/tools/workmux.md); pitfall: [pitfalls/workmux-status-leak.md](pitfalls/workmux-status-leak.md)):
47	
48	1. `dot_ansible/roles/devtools/tasks/main.yml` — binary install (brew tap on macOS; GitHub release `.tar.gz` on Linux)
49	2. `dot_config/workmux/config.yaml` — `status_format: false` is load-bearing
50	3. `dot_config/tmux/theme.catppuccin.conf` — `#{?@workmux_status, #{@workmux_status},}` appended to `@catppuccin_window_text` and `@catppuccin_window_current_text`
51	4. `dot_claude/modify_settings.json` — `Stop`/`SubagentStop`/`UserPromptSubmit`/`Notification` hooks calling `workmux set-window-status` (hook-aware merger preserves CodeIsland entries)
52	5. `dot_config/opencode/plugins/workmux-status.ts` + `dot_config/opencode/modify_package.json`
53	6. `dot_config/shell/60_tmux_status.sh` — generic POSIX `tmux_status_set/get/clear/clear_all/list/run` for non-agent producers
54	
55	**Hard rules**: never run `workmux setup` on a managed machine (would write parallel hook entries); never flip `status_format: true` (fights catppuccin's window-text override); never drop the `command -v workmux >/dev/null 2>&1 && … || true` guard in Claude hooks (spams errors on fresh boxes); never drop explicit `set-window-status done` from `Stop`/`SubagentStop` (upstream only ever sets `working`, never clears — that's the by-design leak documented in the pitfall). `wt` (worktrunk, `37_worktrunk.zsh`) and `wm` (workmux, `38_workmux.zsh`) stay distinct — different config formats, killer features, helper files.

68	## Chezmoi templating conventions
69	
70	**Hard rule**: before adding `{{ if eq .profile … }}`, ask if the predicate is auto-detectable. If yes, use `.chezmoi.os` / `.chezmoi.arch` / `.chezmoi.hostname`. `.profile` is for user-role choices only. Values are limited to `macos`, `ubuntu_desktop`, `ubuntu_server` — do **not** introduce new values for OS/arch facts (historical `macos_intel` profile was removed for exactly this reason).
71	
72	**Hard rule — prefer XDG paths.** When a tool supports both a `$HOME`-root dotfile and an XDG path (`~/.config/<tool>/…`), manage the XDG copy (`dot_config/<tool>/…`) to keep `$HOME` tidy; only use a root dotfile when the tool can't read XDG. For tools that error when *both* paths exist (e.g. AeroSpace), also remove the legacy root file via a gated `.chezmoiremove` entry. Full rule + lookup-order caveats: [docs/this_repo/config-conventions.md → A1](docs/this_repo/config-conventions.md).
73	
74	| Predicate | Use |
75	|---|---|
76	| Any macOS | `eq .chezmoi.os "darwin"` |
77	| Any Linux | `eq .chezmoi.os "linux"` |
78	| Apple Silicon | `eq .chezmoi.arch "arm64"` (in darwin scope) or `and (eq .chezmoi.os "darwin") (eq .chezmoi.arch "arm64")` |
79	| Intel Mac | `and (eq .chezmoi.os "darwin") (eq .chezmoi.arch "amd64")` |
80	| Desktop vs headless | `.profile` — `ubuntu_desktop` / `ubuntu_server` |
81	
82	Decision table, before/after examples, `macos_intel` migration: [docs/tools/chezmoi-templating.md](docs/tools/chezmoi-templating.md).
83	
84	## Hard repo invariants
85	
86	### Validate app configs with the app, not just syntax
87	
88	Template rendering / YAML / TOML / JSON syntax is not enough. If the app exposes a config check, parser, dry-run, or debug command, run it against the rendered config before declaring done (e.g. `codex debug …` for `~/.codex/config.toml`; `tmux source-file` / `display-menu` smoke for tmux; `mkdocs build --strict` for docs; for Ansible run the narrowest practical play/tag/check-mode or container smoke — `--syntax-check` alone is a first pass). If a validator cannot be run, say so explicitly in the final report and name the missing command/host/credential.
89	
90	### `primaryShell` choice gates `chsh` only — both shells always deploy
91	
92	`primaryShell` (`zsh` | `bash`, default `zsh`) **only** governs which login shell `chsh` switches to. Both `~/.zshrc`, `~/.bashrc`, `~/.config/{shell,zsh,bash}/` deploy everywhere — users routinely drop into the other shell ad-hoc.
93	
94	**Hard rules**:
95	
96	- Do **not** add `{{ if eq .primaryShell … }}` gates around `dot_zshrc.tmpl`, `dot_bashrc.tmpl`, or `dot_config/{shell,zsh,bash}/**`.
97	- Do **not** gate the zsh / bash ansible roles' **package install** task on `primary_shell` — only `chsh` is gated. macOS bash 5.x brew install + `/etc/shells` whitelist are gated on `primary_shell == "bash"` (zsh-primary mac users skip the brew formula).
98	- Do **not** rely on `$SHELL` — it reflects `/etc/passwd`, lags `chsh` until next login. Use `$ZSH_VERSION` / `$BASH_VERSION`.
99	
100	ble.sh + oh-my-bash 12-step init order in `dot_bashrc.tmpl` is load-bearing: `ble.sh --attach=none` MUST source before bash-preexec/starship; `ble-attach` MUST be the last call before secrets/adhoc; OMB's `autosuggestions` / `syntax-highlighting` / `history-substring-search` plugins MUST be excluded (ble.sh provides natives; double-init causes flicker). Full breakdown: [docs/shells/bash.md](docs/shells/bash.md).
101	
102	### Three-tier user-local override layer
103	
104	User overrides live in **six** untracked files: shared POSIX (`~/.shellrc.adhoc`, `~/.shellrc.secrets`) and per-shell (`~/.zshrc.adhoc`, `~/.bashrc.adhoc`, `~/.config/zsh/secrets.zsh`, `~/.config/bash/secrets.sh`). All six in `.chezmoiignore.tmpl`. Default target: shared. Drop to per-shell only when shell-specific syntax is required.
105	
106	**Load order** in both `dot_zshrc.tmpl` and `dot_bashrc.tmpl`:
107	
108	```
109	managed modules → shared secrets → per-shell secrets → shared adhoc → per-shell adhoc
110	```
111	
112	Secrets before adhoc (so adhoc can read secret vars); shared before per-shell (per-shell wins on conflict).
113	
114	**Hard rules**: never add the shared files to chezmoi management; never auto-stub the `*.secrets` files (empty secrets footgun); the shared adhoc stub heredoc lives in BOTH `dot_zshrc.tmpl` AND `dot_bashrc.tmpl` (first shell to run wins; second sees the file and skips) — keep both heredoc bodies in sync. Full matrix: [docs/shells/adhoc-and-secrets.md](docs/shells/adhoc-and-secrets.md).
115	
116	### `enableVimMode` gates shell + tmux vim, NOT Neovim or editors
117	
118	`enableVimMode` (bool, default `true`) gates **shell modal editing + tmux vim navigation only**. Neovim and every editor config (VSCode/Cursor/Antigravity/Codex/OpenCode/Cursor-CLI) are **never** affected. Full catalog of the 7 gated templated files + 2 first-seed files (`marimo.toml`, btop's `btop.conf`): [docs/this_repo/vim-mode.md](docs/this_repo/vim-mode.md).
119	
120	**Hard rules**:
121	
122	- Do **not** gate anything under `dot_config/nvim/` — Neovim is inherently vim by design.
123	- Do **not** gate editor configs (`.chezmoitemplates/editor/`, `dot_codex/modify_config.toml.tmpl`, `dot_config/opencode/modify_*.json.tmpl`, `dot_cursor/modify_cli-config.json`) — the flag's semantic is shells + tmux only. Editors want vim → install the editor's vim extension.
124	- Do **not** broaden the gate to `bindkey -M viins`/`vicmd` calls inside `dot_config/zsh/tools/*.zsh` — harmless no-ops without zsh-vi-mode loaded.
125	- The `minimal` bundle in `scripts/init/dotfiles_init.py` forces `enableVimMode = False` (CI/Docker). Don't change without explicit user request.
126	- New vim-touched file → follow the "Yes, gate it" / "No, leave it alone" flow in `docs/this_repo/vim-mode.md` → "For maintainers", and add it to the catalog table in that same page.
127	
128	### Install vs upgrade is split on purpose
129	
130	`chezmoi apply` + ansible is **install-only** (`state: present`, `creates:`). Explicit upgrade path: [`scripts/upgrade_tools.sh`](scripts/upgrade_tools.sh) via `just upgrade-*`. `scripts/**` is in `.chezmoiignore.tmpl`, so the upgrade script runs from the repo, never deployed.
131	
132	**Hard rules**:
133	
134	- Do **not** rewrite ansible roles to `state: latest`.
135	- Do **not** add `apt upgrade` / system package bumps to default scope.
136	- **Minimum-version exception**: a role MAY auto-upgrade a single tool inside `chezmoi apply` when it legitimately needs a newer version (e.g. `python_uv_tools` needs `uv >= 0.8.5` for `--with-executables-from`). MUST detect install style (brew vs curl/standalone) and dispatch — never blindly `uv self update` (no-op on brew uv) or `brew upgrade uv` (errors if not a brew formula). Dispatch helper is mirrored in `scripts/upgrade_tools.sh::cat_uv()` and `dot_ansible/roles/python_uv_tools/tasks/main.yml`. See [docs/this_repo/uv-bootstrap.md](docs/this_repo/uv-bootstrap.md), [pitfalls/uv-self-update-homebrew-noop.md](pitfalls/uv-self-update-homebrew-noop.md), [pitfalls/ansible-when-regex-replace-backslash-strip.md](pitfalls/ansible-when-regex-replace-backslash-strip.md).
137	- **`with_executables_from:` entries MUST also declare `extra_binaries:`** in `dot_ansible/roles/python_uv_tools/defaults/main.yml`. Without it the install guard short-circuits on hosts where the primary binary already exists, and entry-point shims are never written (silent missing `jupyter` / `jupyter-notebook` despite `jupyter-lab` present). Audit: `yq '.python_uv_tools[] | select(.with_executables_from) | select(.extra_binaries == null) | .name' …` MUST print nothing. See [pitfalls/uv-tool-install-creates-guard-misses-executables-from.md](pitfalls/uv-tool-install-creates-guard-misses-executables-from.md).
138	- New upgrade category: [docs/this_repo/upgrades.md → Adding a new category](docs/this_repo/upgrades.md). For a tool already managed by brew/uv/npm/cargo/dotnet/gem/mise: do nothing — generic `upgrade` picks it up.
139	
140	### Sudo session is shared across all run-scripts
141	
142	All three `run_*` scripts share one sudo session via `scripts/lib/sudo_shared.sh` — user prompted once at `chezmoi apply` start, reused silently downstream.
143	
144	**Hard rules**:
145	
146	- Do **not** re-implement `sudo -k` / `sudo -v` / TTY-read logic. Call the shared helper.
147	- Do **not** run `sudo -k` (invalidates the cache for the whole flow).
148	- Do **not** register a `trap … EXIT` that removes state (next run-script needs it).
149	- Do **not** read the password into a shell variable. Always `sudo -S <file`.
150	- Do **not** replace `_sudo_spawn_watchdog`'s `setsid`/`nohup` fallback with bare `setsid` — macOS lacks `setsid(1)` in base, the backgrounded failure is silent (redirected to `/dev/null`), and every run-script then re-prompts because `_sudo_state_valid`'s `kill -0` probe finds a dead PID. See [`pitfalls/sudo-shared-setsid-macos.md`](pitfalls/sudo-shared-setsid-macos.md).
151	
152	**Adding a new sudo surface in a run-script**:
153	
154	1. `{{ include "scripts/lib/sudo_shared.sh" }}` near the top of the template.
155	2. Set the `NEED_SUDO` template flag.
156	3. Call `sudo_session_init "yourlabel"`; branch on return code + `sudo_session_skip_reason`.
157	4. Privileged commands via `sudo_run …` or `-e @$CHEZMOI_ANSIBLE_BECOME_FILE` for ansible.
158	
159	**Non-interactive password injection** (used by `scripts/fleet/apply.py` over SSH): `sudo_session_init` adopts `CHEZMOI_SUDO_PASSWORD_FILE` (a 0600 file) instead of prompting on `/dev/tty`. **Never** read `CHEZMOI_SUDO_PASSWORD_FILE` directly — always go through `sudo_session_init`. Full API + state + cleanup model: [docs/this_repo/sudo-session.md](docs/this_repo/sudo-session.md).
160	
161	### fleet-apply counter-intuitive defaults
162	
163	Full docs: [`docs/this_repo/fleet-apply.md`](docs/this_repo/fleet-apply.md). Load-bearing invariants:
164	
165	- **`drift` ≠ `failed`**. When chezmoi can't prompt to overwrite a hand-edited file (no PTY over SSH), the host shows yellow ⚠ `drift` with paths listed — but it does **not** count toward exit code. Don't auto-"fix" drift unless asked. Resolution: hand-fix the remote, or `--force` to let template win.
166	- **`fleet-apply-file PATH` skips `run_*` scripts** (uses `chezmoi apply --exclude=scripts`). Ansible / Brewfile changes will NOT execute — use full `fleet-apply` for ansible iterations.
167	- **`--branch BRANCH` is no-op on local hosts** (the local source dir IS the user's editor working tree). Local hosts log warn and run against working tree as-is. The flag also forces mode to `apply`.
168	- **Install-only by design** (inherits the previous invariant). `just upgrade-*` must run on each host; fleet-apply does NOT broadcast upgrades.
169	- **Process substitution + sentinel are load-bearing**: `> >(tee -a $log) 2>&1 & _cz_pid=$!; wait $_cz_pid; _rc=$?; echo $_rc > $sentinel`. `--status` / `--tail` / `--watch` + SIGHUP trap depend on `$_cz_pid` pointing to chezmoi, not tee. Don't change to a pipeline.
170	- **Conservative drift classifier**: `_classify_drift()` only downgrades stderr lines matching the exact `chezmoi: <path>: could not open a new TTY: open /dev/tty:` fingerprint. Anything unrecognised stays `failed`. Don't broaden without explicit user request — silent downgrades hide real errors.
171	- **`fleet-status` ≠ `fleet-apply-status`** — easy to confuse:
172	  - `just fleet-status` → **pre-flight readiness probe** (states: `up-to-date`, `behind`, `ahead`, `dirty`, `drift`, `ready-to-update`, `busy`, `init-in-progress`, `toml-mismatch`, `not-init`, `no-source`, `no-chezmoi`, `unreachable`). Run **before** `fleet-apply`. Always exits 0; use `--readiness-json | jq` for scripted gates. `fleet-status-quick` skips remote `git fetch`.
173	  - `just fleet-apply-status` → **process-liveness probe** of `~/.cache/fleet-apply/<host>.{pid,sentinel,log}`. Run **during/after**. Pairs with `fleet-apply-tail` / `fleet-apply-watch` / `fleet-apply-kill`.
174	  - `toml-mismatch` catches a remote's `chezmoi.toml` missing prompt keys that current `.chezmoi.toml.tmpl` requires, via static `_PROMPT_KEY_RE` comparison — `chezmoi dump-config` cannot be used (would re-evaluate the very template we're inspecting).
175	  - `fleet-edit` + `fleet-status` are forgiving (auto-seed / exit 0 with hint); `fleet-apply` keeps strict exit-2 on missing inventory. Don't unify.
176	
177	### `modify_` and `create_` prefix semantics
178	
179	- **`modify_`** files are executable scripts: chezmoi pipes current target contents to stdin, expects new contents on stdout. Used for `~/.claude/settings.json` (jq overlay), editor `settings.json` (VSCode/Cursor/Antigravity), agent CLI configs (`~/.cursor/cli-config.json`, `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json`, `~/.codex/config.toml`), `~/.config/herdr/config.toml` (tomlkit overlay — managed tables enforced, herdr's runtime writeback preserved), and `~/.gitconfig` (preserves `[credential "<URL>"]` blocks injected by `gh auth setup-git` so the gh-managed absolute path to the local `gh` binary — different on Intel mac / Apple Silicon / Linuxbrew — survives `chezmoi apply`). **Never** `chezmoi add` a `modify_` target — it would overwrite the script with the live file.
180	- **`create_`** files seed once; chezmoi never touches contents after. Used for `~/.config/nvim/lazy-lock.json` and editor `keybindings.json`. Refresh baseline by copying directly: `cp <target> "$(chezmoi source-path <target>)"`. `chezmoi add` strips the prefix; `chezmoi re-add` silently skips.
181	
182	Case studies + presence-gating in `.chezmoiignore.tmpl`: [docs/tools/chezmoi-prefixes.md](docs/tools/chezmoi-prefixes.md). Three agent CLI overlays (incl. the Claude hook-aware merger that coexists with [CodeIsland](https://github.com/wxtsky/CodeIsland)'s auto-installed hook entries without ping-ponging): [docs/tools/agent-overlays.md](docs/tools/agent-overlays.md).
183	
184	### Tmux popup menu: ≥ 3.3 required + must fit terminal height
185	
186	The popup menu (bound to `prefix + Space` and `prefix + e`) is **generated** by `~/.config/tmux/menu.sh`, not inline in `keybindings.conf`. Two unrelated tmux quirks force this:
187	
188	1. **Position clamping (tmux ≥ 3.3)**: `display-menu -x R -y P` is silently suppressed on tmux 3.2a (Ubuntu 22.04 apt) when it would place the menu past the terminal edge. tmux 3.3+ clamps. `devtools` role auto-upgrades on Debian/Ubuntu (Linuxbrew first, else [`nelsonenzo/tmux-appimage`](https://github.com/nelsonenzo/tmux-appimage) extracted to `~/.local/share/tmux-appimage/` with a `~/.local/bin/tmux` shim). Run `tmux kill-server` once after — running servers keep the old binary in memory.
189	2. **Menu-too-tall silent failure (all versions)**: `display-menu` does **not** paginate. Taller than terminal → entire popup suppressed, no error, nothing in `tmux show-messages`. `man tmux`: _"If the menu is too large to fit on the terminal, it is not displayed."_ Misdiagnosed for hours as a CSI-u keysym bug after a 50-row flat menu started failing on smaller heights.
190	
191	**Hard rules**:
192	
193	- **Top menu cap ≈ 14 rows**. Generator reads `#{client_height}` and tier-trims; retest at heights 14 / 22 / 60 when changing tiers. Push lower-frequency items into category submenus.
194	- **Submenus = separate scripts**, each `exec tmux display-menu …`. Quoting context resets per script.
195	- **Complex commands** (anything with `{`, `}`, `;`, backticks, nested fzf binds) MUST live in their own script. tmux's parser treats `{}` / `;` as command-block delimiters even inside `'…'` inside `"…"`, silently aborting parse.
196	- **Test by shrinking the terminal vertically**. Full-height verification does not catch the height-fit failure.
197	
198	See `pitfalls/tmux-display-menu-silent-fail.md` (red herrings included) and `pitfalls/yazi-tmux-popup-crash.md`.
199	
200	### Key tmux settings for coding agents
201	
202	Non-obvious settings other tools depend on; do not remove without checking:
203	
204	- `extended-keys on` + `terminal-features 'xterm*:extkeys'` — forwards Shift+Enter, Ctrl+Enter, Ctrl+/, Ctrl+digit to inner apps (Claude Code, Neovim, …). **Never use `always`** — re-encodes EVERY `Ctrl+letter` as CSI-u including the LF (Ctrl+J) embedded in pasted multi-line text → ble.sh inserts `^[[106;5u` literally instead of newline. See `pitfalls/tmux-extended-keys-always-paste.md`.
205	- `escape-time 0` — eliminates ESC delay for Neovim.
206	- `set-clipboard on` + `terminal-features …:clipboard` (for `xterm*`, `ghostty*`, `alacritty*`) — OSC 52 over SSH without terminfo `Ms`. Paired with SSH-conditional `vim.g.clipboard = vim.ui.clipboard.osc52` in `dot_config/nvim/lua/config/options.lua`. See [docs/tools/tmux/README.md → OSC 52 Clipboard](docs/tools/tmux/README.md).
207	- `allow-passthrough on` — OSC passthrough for terminal images.
208	- macOS terminals must send Option as Meta/Esc+ for `M-` keybindings (theme switching, layouts, fine resize). Ghostty/cmux: `macos-option-as-alt = left` in `dot_config/ghostty/config`. See [docs/tools/ghostty.md](docs/tools/ghostty.md).
209	
210	Full tmux config breakdown / theme switching / keybindings / troubleshooting: [docs/tools/tmux/](docs/tools/tmux/).
211	
212	### Zellij `default_mode "locked"`
213	
214	`dot_config/zellij/config.kdl` uses `default_mode "locked"` so all keys pass through to inner apps by default. `Ctrl+G` to unlock Zellij commands. First Zellij launch (no existing config): select the "Unlock-First (non-colliding)" keybinding preset.
215

```text
732	| `run-for DURATION CMD...` | function | `dot_config/shell/10_aliases.sh` | Time-box any command: run for DURATION (`5m`/`30s`/bare secs) then send SIGINT (trap-summary friendly), SIGKILL after a grace. Wraps GNU `timeout`/`gtimeout` (coreutils). Exit `124` = time-box hit |
733	| `source-rc` | function | `dot_config/shell/10_aliases.sh` | Re-source the current shell's rc (`~/.zshrc` or `~/.bashrc`, auto-detected via `$ZSH_VERSION`/`$BASH_VERSION`) **in place** — pick up new aliases/functions after `chezmoi apply` without a fresh login shell. Lighter counterpart to the `exec`-based `cas`/`cau`; inherits the same caveats as a manual `source ~/.zshrc`. On zsh it force-reinitializes `zsh-vi-mode` after re-sourcing so vim mode survives the reload — OMZ's unconditional `bindkey -e` + zsh-vi-mode's once-only init guard otherwise silently drop you back to emacs keys ([pitfall](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/blob/main/pitfalls/zsh-vim-mode-lost-after-source-rc.md)) |
734	| `reload` | alias | `dot_config/shell/10_aliases.sh` | Short alias for `source-rc`. Now cross-shell (previously bash-only `. ~/.bashrc`) |
735	| `tldrf` | function | `dot_config/shell/28_tldr.sh` | `tldr` with language fallback: zh_TW → zh → en *(requires tldr)* |
736	| `abspath [-r] [-t] [PATH...]` | function | `dot_config/shell/58_abspath.sh` | Print absolute path(s): no args → logical cwd (like `pwd`); `PATH...` → one absolute path per line. Logical by default (normalizes `.`/`..`, keeps symlinks, existence not required); `-r`/`--resolve` → physical path (follows symlinks, must exist); `-t`/`--tilde` → abbreviate a `$HOME`-rooted result to `~`. stdout stays pipe-clean, so `abspath FILE \| x copy` grabs a path to the clipboard (fills the `realpath FILE \| x copy` hint in `x`'s help). Requires python3 |
```

```text
1	# ~/.config/shell/58_abspath.sh
2	# Source: dot_config/shell/58_abspath.sh (managed by chezmoi)
3	#
4	# `abspath` — print absolute path(s), POSIX, sourced by both zsh and bash.
5	#   - no args  -> behaves like `pwd` (LOGICAL cwd, symlinks intact)
6	#   - FILE...  -> one absolute path per line
7	#   -r/--resolve : resolve symlinks to the physical path (requires existence)
8	#   -t/--tilde   : abbreviate a $HOME-rooted result to `~`
9	# Pairs with the `x` clipboard CLI:  abspath FILE | x copy
10	#
11	# stdout is pipe-clean (paths only); usage/errors go to stderr.
12	#
13	# Logical base MUST be the shell's $PWD, not python's os.getcwd() (which is
14	# physical / symlink-resolved) — otherwise no-arg output wouldn't equal `pwd`.
15	
16	_abspath_usage() {
17	    printf '%s\n' \
18	        "Usage: abspath [-r|--resolve] [-t|--tilde] [--] [PATH...]" \
19	        "  (no PATH) print the current directory, like pwd" \
20	        "  PATH...   print each path's absolute form, one per line" \
21	        "  -r        resolve symlinks to the physical path (must exist)" \
22	        "  -t        abbreviate a \$HOME-rooted result to ~" \
23	        "Examples:" \
24	        "  abspath                 # == pwd" \
25	        "  abspath foo.py ../bar   # absolute paths" \
26	        "  abspath -t ~/notes.md   # ~/notes.md" \
27	        "  abspath foo.py | x copy"
28	}
29	
30	abspath() {
31	    _ap_resolve=0
32	    _ap_tilde=0
33	    while [ "$#" -gt 0 ]; do
34	        case "$1" in
35	            -r|--resolve) _ap_resolve=1; shift ;;
36	            -t|--tilde)   _ap_tilde=1;   shift ;;
37	            -h|--help)    _abspath_usage; unset _ap_resolve _ap_tilde; return 0 ;;
38	            --)           shift; break ;;
39	            -*)           printf 'abspath: unknown option: %s\n' "$1" >&2
40	                          _abspath_usage >&2
41	                          unset _ap_resolve _ap_tilde; return 2 ;;
42	            *)            break ;;
43	        esac
44	    done
45	
46	    if ! command -v python3 >/dev/null 2>&1; then
47	        printf 'abspath: python3 required for path normalization\n' >&2
48	        unset _ap_resolve _ap_tilde; return 127
49	    fi
50	
51	    ABSPATH_BASE="$PWD" ABSPATH_RESOLVE="$_ap_resolve" ABSPATH_TILDE="$_ap_tilde" \
52	        python3 - "$@" <<'PY'
53	import os, sys
54	
55	base    = os.environ.get("ABSPATH_BASE") or os.getcwd()
56	resolve = os.environ.get("ABSPATH_RESOLVE") == "1"
57	tilde   = os.environ.get("ABSPATH_TILDE") == "1"
58	home    = os.path.expanduser("~")
59	args    = sys.argv[1:] or ["."]          # no args -> current dir, like pwd
60	rc = 0
61	
62	def abbrev(p):
63	    if not tilde:
64	        return p
65	    if p == home:
66	        return "~"
67	    if p.startswith(home + os.sep):
68	        return "~" + p[len(home):]
69	    return p
70	
71	for a in args:
72	    joined = a if os.path.isabs(a) else os.path.join(base, a)
73	    if resolve:
74	        p = os.path.realpath(joined)     # physical; follows symlinks
75	        if not os.path.exists(p):
76	            sys.stderr.write("abspath: no such file or directory: %s\n" % a)
77	            rc = 1
78	            continue
79	    else:
80	        p = os.path.normpath(joined)     # lexical; keeps symlinks, no existence req.
81	    print(abbrev(p))
82	
83	sys.exit(rc)
84	PY
85	    _ap_rc=$?
86	    unset _ap_resolve _ap_tilde
87	    return "$_ap_rc"
88	}
89
```

```text
1	# ~/.config/shell/63_tmux_path.sh
2	# Source: dot_config/shell/63_tmux_path.sh (managed by chezmoi)
3	#
4	# `tpath` — print + copy the CURRENT tmux pane's address, POSIX, sourced by
5	# both zsh and bash. Copies the readable target `session:window.pane` (e.g.
6	# `main:2.1`) to the system clipboard via tmux's OSC 52 bridge, and prints
7	# `target` / `pane_id` / `cwd` to stdout for reference.
8	#
9	# Why: when a human and an AI agent share a tmux session, you need a quick way
10	# to grab the pane you're looking at — to reconnect later, or to tell the agent
11	# "operate on THIS pane" (`tmux capture-pane -pt <target>` /
12	# `tmux send-keys -t <target> ...`). The stable `pane_id` (%N, survives
13	# window/pane reordering) and cwd are printed alongside so you can paste the
14	# richer form into an agent chat when the readable target isn't enough.
15	#
16	# GUI/keyboard equivalents (same "Copy pane path" action):
17	#   - right-click a pane → "Copy pane path"   (MouseDown3Pane menu)
18	#   - prefix + M-p → "Copy pane path"          (menu-pane.sh)
19	#   - prefix + P                               (direct keybinding)
20	# All defined in dot_config/tmux/keybindings.conf.tmpl + menu-pane.sh.
21	#
22	# stdout is kept pipe-clean (`tpath | head -1` yields the target line); the
23	# "copied" confirmation goes to stderr.
24	
25	# Skip silently if tmux isn't on PATH (cron, headless SSH, fresh box).
26	command -v tmux >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 0
27	
28	# tpath — copy current pane's session:window.pane to clipboard, print details.
29	tpath() {
30	    if [ -z "${TMUX:-}" ]; then
31	        printf 'tpath: not inside a tmux session\n' >&2
32	        return 1
33	    fi
34	
35	    _tpath_target=$(tmux display-message -p '#{session_name}:#{window_index}.#{pane_index}')
36	    _tpath_id=$(tmux display-message -p '#{pane_id}')
37	    _tpath_cwd=$(tmux display-message -p '#{pane_current_path}')
38	
39	    # Copy ONLY the readable target. `set-buffer -w` loads tmux's paste buffer
40	    # AND forwards via OSC 52 (needs `set-clipboard on` in common.conf) — works
41	    # over SSH without shelling out to pbcopy/xclip on the remote host.
42	    tmux set-buffer -w "$_tpath_target"
43	
44	    printf 'target : %s\n' "$_tpath_target"
45	    printf 'pane_id: %s\n' "$_tpath_id"
46	    printf 'cwd    : %s\n' "$_tpath_cwd"
47	    printf 'Copied pane path: %s\n' "$_tpath_target" >&2
48	
49	    unset _tpath_target _tpath_id _tpath_cwd
50	}
```

 `./docs/neovim/copy-reference.md`

```text
1	# Copy Cursor-style file references (`@file:line`)
2	
3	Four Neovim keymaps that copy a **Cursor / Claude Code style file reference** —
4	`@path`, `@path:12`, or `@path:12-40` — to the system clipboard, built from the
5	current buffer plus the cursor line (normal mode), the visual selection
6	(visual mode), or — in a file explorer — the node under the cursor. The `@` triggers the agent's file-mention and the `:line[-line]`
7	points it at exact code, so you paste an exact pointer instead of retyping paths
8	and line numbers by hand.
9	
10	All four live in `lua/config/keymaps.lua` under a `<leader>y` ("copy ref")
11	which-key group. Press `<leader>y` (Space then `y`) to see them.
12	
13	## Keymaps
14	
15	`<leader>` = Space. Every key works in **normal** and **visual** mode.
16	
17	| Keymap | Path flavor | Normal mode (cursor line) | Visual mode (selection) |
18	|--------|-------------|---------------------------|-------------------------|
19	| `<leader>yr` | project-relative | `@rel/path:12` | `@rel/path:12-40` |
20	| `<leader>ya` | machine-absolute | `@/abs/path:12` | `@/abs/path:12-40` |
21	| `<leader>yf` | project-relative | `@rel/path` (no line) | `@rel/path` (no line) |
22	| `<leader>yF` | machine-absolute | `@/abs/path` (no line) | `@/abs/path` (no line) |
23	
24	Mnemonic: `r`elative / `a`bsolute carry the line; `f`ile-only (capital `F` =
25	absolute) is the bare path. Together the four cover all three reference shapes:
26	
27	- `@file` → `<leader>yf`
28	- `@file:line` → `<leader>yr` in normal mode
29	- `@file:line1-line2` → `<leader>yr` in visual mode
30	
31	A single-line visual selection collapses `:12-12` → `:12`. After copying in
32	visual mode the mapping leaves visual mode and shows a `Copied @…` toast.
33	
34	## Path flavors
35	
36	- **Relative** (`yr` / `yf`) is resolved against the **git root**
37	  (`LazyVim.root.git()` — the same root used by [Floating TUI](floating-tui.md)).
38	  A file outside the git root falls back to a `~` / cwd-relative path.
39	- **Absolute** (`ya` / `yF`) is the full machine path (`expand("%:p")`), with no
40	  symlink resolution.
41	
42	Relative is usually what you want for Claude Code (it operates inside the
43	project); absolute is for files outside the repo, or when a tool needs the full
44	path.
45	
46	## File explorers (neo-tree / snacks)
47	
48	Trigger a keymap while focused in a **file-explorer** buffer and the reference
49	points at the **node under the cursor** instead (no line number) — e.g.
50	`<leader>yf` on a tree entry copies `@rel/path/to/that/file`. This mirrors
51	neo-tree's own `Y` (copy path).
52	
53	- **neo-tree** is supported today (resolves the node via neo-tree's manager API).
54	- **snacks explorer** — LazyVim's neo-tree successor — is handled best-effort, so
55	  the keymaps keep working after that migration.
56	- Any other special buffer (terminal, help, quickfix, an unknown explorer, an
57	  unnamed buffer) is safely rejected with a `copy-ref: no file under cursor here`
58	  warning — never a bogus `@neo-tree filesystem [1]`.
59	
60	## Implementation notes
61	
62	The feature is a small `copy_ref_target()` + `copy_reference()` helper pair plus
63	four `vim.keymap.set({ "n", "x" }, …)` calls in `lua/config/keymaps.lua`. It
64	reuses, with no new dependencies:
65	
66	- `LazyVim.root.git()` — git-root detection.
67	- `vim.fs.relpath(root, abspath)` — built-in relative-path computation.
68	- `vim.fn.setreg("+", ref)` — respects the OSC 52 clipboard provider configured
69	  in `lua/config/options.lua`, so it copies into your local terminal clipboard
70	  even over SSH. Do **not** shell out to `pbcopy` — that bypasses OSC 52. See
71	  [Clipboard](../tools/clipboard.md).
72	- Visual range via `vim.fn.line(".")` / `vim.fn.line("v")` — the same pattern the
73	  gitsigns stage-selection maps use.
74	
75	Buffer resolution lives in a `copy_ref_target()` helper: real file buffers
76	(empty `buftype`) yield the file plus line context; known explorers yield the
77	node under the cursor; everything else returns `nil` and the caller warns.
78	Explorer lookups are `pcall`-wrapped so a changed or absent API degrades to that
79	warning instead of crashing or emitting a garbage path. A deleted cwd is likewise
80	guarded with `pcall` (avoids the Neovim 0.12 `vim.fs.find` ENOENT trap) and falls
81	back to a relative path.
82	
83	## Why `<leader>y`
84	
85	`<leader>y` was an unused prefix. The AI keymaps under `<leader>a` are already
86	crowded — avante and claudecode both bind many `<leader>a…` keys and even
87	collide with each other — so a fresh `y` ("yank / copy") group keeps these
88	reference-copy actions clear of that contention and easy to find in which-key.
89	
90	To change or extend the set, edit the `copy_reference` helper and the
91	`vim.keymap.set` block in `lua/config/keymaps.lua`.
92
```
</details></tool-use>

```text
3	# app-* helpers — graceful control of macOS GUI apps via osascript / Apple Events.
4	#
5	# Why not `killall`? `killall AppName` sends SIGTERM and most GUI apps don't
6	# register a handler, so containers / unsaved buffers / background sync just
7	# die. `osascript -e 'tell application "X" to quit'` sends the Quit Apple
8	# Event — the same thing ⌘Q does — so the app tears down cleanly. Matters
9	# for OrbStack / Docker Desktop / Slack / any app with state.
10	#
11	# Frozen-app detection (`appresponsive`) is best-effort: macOS exposes the
12	# "Not Responding" flag only via Activity Monitor's private SPI. The public
13	# proxy is "send a no-op Apple Event with a short timeout — if it throws,
14	# the app is hung." False positives happen on apps mid-launch.
15	#
16	# All helpers take an app NAME (e.g. `OrbStack`, `Google Chrome`), not a
17	# bundle ID. `$1` is passed via osascript's `argv` so spaces and quotes in
18	# app names are handled correctly without shell-escaping gymnastics.
19	#
20	# Linux counterpart: dot_config/shell/56_linux_apps.sh.tmpl. Same public
21	# verb names (appquit / applaunch / appactivate / apprestart / apprunning /
22	# applist / appresponsive) but a different backend — gtk-launch + pkill -TERM
23	# + optional GNOME window-calls extension. Cross-platform muscle memory by
24	# design; per-platform gaps documented in
25	# backlog/linux-desktop-app-control.md (Alt+H "hide" is mac-only — Linux
26	# can't hide windows without compositor IPC).
```

```text
# Custom Aliases & Shell Functions

Quick reference for custom aliases and shell functions defined in this dotfiles repo. Available in zsh, bash, or both — the source file path tells you which:

- `dot_config/shell/*.sh` — POSIX layer, sourced by **both** `~/.zshrc` and `~/.bashrc`.
- `dot_config/zsh/*.zsh` (or `tools/*.zsh`) — **zsh-only**.
- `dot_config/bash/*.bash` — **bash-only**.
```

# Findings: `abspath` and the repo's clipboard-copy helpers

## 1. `abspath` — the command you referenced

**File:** `/Users/david/.local/share/chezmoi/dot_config/shell/58_abspath.sh` (entire file, 89 lines)
- Usage/help helper `_abspath_usage`: **lines 16–28**
- Function `abspath`: **lines 30–88** (arg parsing 33–44; python3 guard 46–49; python core 51–84)

**What it does:** Prints absolute path(s) to **stdout only** — it does **not** copy to the clipboard itself. No args → logical `$PWD` (like `pwd`); `PATH...` → one absolute path per line. `-r`/`--resolve` = physical path via `os.path.realpath` (must exist); `-t`/`--tilde` = abbreviate `$HOME`-rooted result to `~`. Normalization is done by an inline `python3` heredoc (hard dependency; returns 127 if python3 missing). stdout is kept pipe-clean; usage/errors go to stderr.

**Clipboard relationship:** It is explicitly designed to *pipe into* the clipboard, not copy directly. The header comment (line 9) and usage example (line 27) both show the canonical idiom:
```sh
abspath FILE | x copy
```
This deliberately fills the `realpath FILE | x copy` hint in the `x` CLI's own help (see below).

**Scope:** **Shared POSIX**, sourced by *both* zsh and bash. Files matching `dot_config/shell/*.sh` are the repo's shared POSIX layer (confirmed in `dot_zshrc.tmpl:120-122` "Used for the shared POSIX layer (.sh) and the zsh-only layer (.zsh)" and `dot_bashrc.tmpl:198`). The script uses only POSIX `sh` constructs (`case`, `command -v`, `[ ]`, `$#`), no bashisms/zshisms.

**Tab-completion:** **None defined.** Grep for `abspath`/`compdef abspath`/`complete ... abspath` across `dot_config/bash/` and `dot_config/zsh/` returned nothing. Because `abspath` takes filesystem paths, the shells' default file-name completion applies with no custom setup.

**Row in `docs/shells/aliases.md`:** present at **line 736** (in the "Shell Utilities" table, header at line 727):
```
| `abspath [-r] [-t] [PATH...]` | function | `dot_config/shell/58_abspath.sh` | Print absolute path(s): no args → logical cwd (like `pwd`); `PATH...` → one absolute path per line. Logical by default (normalizes `.`/`..`, keeps symlinks, existence not required); `-r`/`--resolve` → physical path (follows symlinks, must exist); `-t`/`--tilde` → abbreviate a `$HOME`-rooted result to `~`. stdout stays pipe-clean, so `abspath FILE \| x copy` grabs a path to the clipboard (fills the `realpath FILE \| x copy` hint in `x`'s help). Requires python3 |
```

**Design doc (context):** `/Users/david/.local/share/chezmoi/.claude/plans/unify-absolute-path-pwd-hidden-simon.md` is the plan that produced this function. No `relpath`, `cwdpath`, or `copypath` shell command exists anywhere in the repo — I searched exhaustively. (The only `relpath`/`abspath` hits outside this file are Lua — `vim.fs.relpath` — in `docs/neovim/copy-reference.md` and `.claude/plans/cursor-reference-*.md`, unrelated to the shell.)

## 2. Canonical way this repo copies text to the clipboard from the shell: the `x` CLI

**File:** `/Users/david/.local/share/chezmoi/dot_dotfiles/bin/executable_x` → deployed to `~/.dotfiles/bin/x` (on PATH). This is the repo's single blessed clipboard/open wrapper. Subcommands: `x copy [--force] [FILE]`, `x copy-file [--force] PATH...`, `x paste`, `x open TARGET`.

**Text copy cascade — `copy_backend()`, lines 141–189.** Reads stdin (or a file) and tries backends in priority order, first available wins:
1. `clip.exe` (WSL) — 142–148
2. `pbcopy` (macOS) — 150–156
3. `wl-copy` (Wayland, if `$WAYLAND_DISPLAY`) — 158–164
4. `xclip -selection clipboard` (X11, if `$DISPLAY`) — 166–172
5. `xsel --clipboard --input` (X11) — 174–180
6. **OSC 52 fallback** via `osc52_copy` — 182–185 (works over SSH, no display needed)

**OSC 52 implementation — `osc52_copy()`, lines 61–76** (verbatim; this is the repo's canonical OSC 52 emitter for arbitrary text):
```bash
osc52_copy() {
    [[ -w /dev/tty ]] || return 1
    command -v base64 >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 1

    local data
    data="$(base64 | tr -d '\n')"
    [[ -n "$data" ]] || return 0

    if [[ -n "${TMUX:-}" ]]; then
        # shellcheck disable=SC1003 # printf consumes the backslash escapes.
        printf '\033Ptmux;\033\033]52;c;%s\033\033\\\033\\' "$data" > /dev/tty
    else
        # shellcheck disable=SC1003 # printf consumes the backslash escapes.
        printf '\033]52;c;%s\033\\' "$data" > /dev/tty
    fi
}
```
It base64-encodes stdin and writes the OSC 52 escape to `/dev/tty` (so it survives an outer pipeline), with a tmux passthrough (`\033Ptmux;...`) wrapper when `$TMUX` is set.

Note: `x copy` also refuses SSH private-key material by default (`is_sensitive_file`, lines 87–123; enforced 405–409) unless `--force`. `x copy-file` (lines 191–258) copies desktop *file objects* (macOS JXA `NSPasteboard.writeObjects`, or Linux `x-special/gnome-copied-files`) — that's a different feature from text copy and is explicitly unavailable over OSC 52.

**Tab-completion for `x`:** `dot_config/bash/49_x_completion.bash` and `dot_config/zsh/tools/49_x_completion.zsh`.

**Docs:** `docs/tools/clipboard.md` is the reference for how OSC 52 clipboard sync is wired across terminal / tmux / Neovim / the `x` CLI.

## 3. Other clipboard/path-copy helpers (related surface)

## 2. Canonical way this repo copies text to the clipboard from the shell: the `x` CLI

**File:** `/Users/david/.local/share/chezmoi/dot_dotfiles/bin/executable_x` → deployed to `~/.dotfiles/bin/x` (on PATH). This is the repo's single blessed clipboard/open wrapper. Subcommands: `x copy [--force] [FILE]`, `x copy-file [--force] PATH...`, `x paste`, `x open TARGET`.

**Text copy cascade — `copy_backend()`, lines 141–189.** Reads stdin (or a file) and tries backends in priority order, first available wins:
1. `clip.exe` (WSL) — 142–148
2. `pbcopy` (macOS) — 150–156
3. `wl-copy` (Wayland, if `$WAYLAND_DISPLAY`) — 158–164
4. `xclip -selection clipboard` (X11, if `$DISPLAY`) — 166–172
5. `xsel --clipboard --input` (X11) — 174–180
6. **OSC 52 fallback** via `osc52_copy` — 182–185 (works over SSH, no display needed)

**OSC 52 implementation — `osc52_copy()`, lines 61–76** (verbatim; this is the repo's canonical OSC 52 emitter for arbitrary text):
```bash
osc52_copy() {
    [[ -w /dev/tty ]] || return 1
    command -v base64 &gt;/dev/null 2&gt;&amp;1 || return 1

    local data
    data="$(base64 | tr -d '\n')"
    [[ -n "$data" ]] || return 0

    if [[ -n "${TMUX:-}" ]]; then
        # shellcheck disable=SC1003 # printf consumes the backslash escapes.
        printf '\033Ptmux;\033\033]52;c;%s\033\033\\\033\\' "$data" &gt; /dev/tty
    else
        # shellcheck disable=SC1003 # printf consumes the backslash escapes.
        printf '\033]52;c;%s\033\\' "$data" &gt; /dev/tty
    fi
}
```
It base64-encodes stdin and writes the OSC 52 escape to `/dev/tty` (so it survives an outer pipeline), with a tmux passthrough (`\033Ptmux;...`) wrapper when `$TMUX` is set.

Note: `x copy` also refuses SSH private-key material by default (`is_sensitive_file`, lines 87–123; enforced 405–409) unless `--force`. `x copy-file` (lines 191–258) copies desktop *file objects* (macOS JXA `NSPasteboard.writeObjects`, or Linux `x-special/gnome-copied-files`) — that's a different feature from text copy and is explicitly unavailable over OSC 52.

## Verbatim source

### `copy_reference()` — the formatting core — `keymaps.lua:57-99`

```lua
local function copy_reference(opts)
  local abspath, allow_line = copy_ref_target()
  if not abspath then
    vim.notify("copy-ref: no file under cursor here", vim.log.levels.WARN)
    return
  end

  -- path component
  local path
  if opts.absolute then
    path = abspath
  else
    -- pcall guards the nvim-0.12 vim.fs.find ENOENT-on-nil-cwd trap
    -- (pitfalls/nvim-fs-find-enoent-stale-cwd.md)
    local ok, root = pcall(function()
      return LazyVim.root.git()
    end)
    path = (ok and root and vim.fs.relpath(root, abspath)) or vim.fn.fnamemodify(abspath, ":~:.")
  end

  -- line component (only meaningful in a real file buffer)
  local mode = vim.fn.mode()
  local visual = mode == "v" or mode == "V" or mode == "\22"
  local suffix = ""
  if opts.lines and allow_line then
    if visual then
      local a, b = vim.fn.line("."), vim.fn.line("v")
      if a > b then
        a, b = b, a
      end
      suffix = (a == b) and (":" .. a) or (":" .. a .. "-" .. b)
    else
      suffix = ":" .. vim.fn.line(".")
    end
  end
  if visual then
    vim.api.nvim_feedkeys(vim.keycode("<Esc>"), "n", false) -- leave visual mode
  end

  local ref = "@" .. path .. suffix
  vim.fn.setreg("+", ref)
  vim.notify("Copied " .. ref, vim.log.levels.INFO)
end
```

### `copy_ref_target()` — buffer/path resolution — `keymaps.lua:24-55`

The part relevant to a shell command is the real-file-buffer branch (explorer branches are Neovim-specific):

```lua
local function copy_ref_target()
  if vim.bo.buftype == "" then
    local name = vim.api.nvim_buf_get_name(0)
    if name ~= "" then
      return vim.fn.fnamemodify(name, ":p"), true   -- absolute path, no symlink resolution; allow_line = true
    end
    return nil
  end
  ...
```

`fnamemodify(name, ":p")` is the machine-absolute path with **no symlink resolution** (equivalent to `expand("%:p")`).

### Keymaps — `keymaps.lua:105-116`

```lua
vim.keymap.set({ "n", "x" }, "<leader>yr", function() copy_reference({ lines = true }) end,                    { desc = "Ref: relative + line" })
vim.keymap.set({ "n", "x" }, "<leader>ya", function() copy_reference({ lines = true, absolute = true }) end,   { desc = "Ref: absolute + line" })
vim.keymap.set({ "n", "x" }, "<leader>yf", function() copy_reference({}) end,                                  { desc = "Ref: relative (file only)" })
vim.keymap.set({ "n", "x" }, "<leader>yF", function() copy_reference({ absolute = true }) end,                 { desc = "Ref: absolute (file only)" })
```

So: `absolute` toggles path flavor; `lines` toggles whether a `:line` suffix is appended.

## Path-flavor logic (the three flavors)

### 1. Project-relative (git root) — `keymaps.lua:71-74`

```lua
local ok, root = pcall(function() return LazyVim.root.git() end)
path = (ok and root and vim.fs.relpath(root, abspath)) or vim.fn.fnamemodify(abspath, ":~:.")
```

`LazyVim.root.git()` is defined at `/System/Volumes/Data/Users/david/.local/share/nvim/lazy/LazyVim/lua/lazyvim/util/root.lua:193-198`:

```lua
function M.git()
  local root = M.get()
  local git_root = vim.fs.find(".git", { path = root, upward = true })[1]
  local ret = git_root and vim.fn.fnamemodify(git_root, ":h") or root
  return ret
end
```

How the git root is found: start from `M.get()` (LazyVim's detected root — lsp / `.git` / cwd, see `root.lua:178-191`), walk **upward** looking for a `.git` entry (`vim.fs.find(..., upward=true)`), then take its parent directory (`:h`). If no `.git` is found it returns the detected root unchanged.

The relative path itself is computed by the built-in `vim.fs.relpath(root, abspath)` — it returns `abspath` expressed relative to `root` (e.g. `lua/config/keymaps.lua`), **with no leading `./`**, or `nil` if `abspath` is not inside `root`.

Important symlink nuance for faithful shell reproduction: `M.get()` returns a **realpath-resolved** root — every candidate path passes through `M.realpath()` (`root.lua:111`), which calls `vim.uv.fs_realpath()` (`root.lua:77-83`). But `abspath` is **not** symlink-resolved. So `vim.fs.relpath` succeeds only when `abspath` lexically sits under the resolved root. In a shell, `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` likewise returns a symlink-resolved path, so to match you should resolve the file path (or at least compare in the same symlink-space) before computing the relative segment — otherwise you'll hit the fallback more often than Neovim does.

### 2. Machine-absolute — `keymaps.lua:66-67`

```lua
if opts.absolute then
  path = abspath
```

Just the raw absolute path from `fnamemodify(name, ":p")` — no symlink resolution.

### 3. Fallback (file outside git root) — `keymaps.lua:74`

When `LazyVim.root.git()` fails/returns nil, OR `vim.fs.relpath` returns nil (file not under root):

```lua
path = vim.fn.fnamemodify(abspath, ":~:.")
```

`:~:.` means: first make it relative to **cwd** if possible (`:.`), else make it relative to **home** with a `~` prefix (`:~`), else leave absolute. So a file under cwd → `subdir/file.txt`; a file under `$HOME` but outside cwd → `~/somewhere/file.txt`; otherwise the absolute path.

## `@` prefix and line suffix

- Prefix: literally `"@" .. path .. suffix` (`keymaps.lua:96`). Always a single leading `@`, no space.
- Suffix rules (`keymaps.lua:80-91`), only applied when `opts.lines` is set **and** `allow_line` is true (i.e. a real file buffer, not an explorer node):
  - **Normal mode:** `":" .. vim.fn.line(".")` → `:12` (current cursor line).
  - **Visual mode:** takes both ends `vim.fn.line(".")` and `vim.fn.line("v")`, sorts so `a <= b`, then:
    - `a == b` → `":" .. a` (single-line selection collapses `:12-12` → `:12`)
    - else → `":" .. a .. "-" .. b` → `:12-40`
  - When `opts.lines` is false (`yf`/`yF`) the suffix stays `""` → bare `@path`.

## Clipboard

Confirmed: `vim.fn.setreg("+", ref)` at `keymaps.lua:97`. No `pbcopy` shell-out. It writes to the `+` register, which is routed through OSC 52 by the provider configured in `/Users/david/.local/share/chezmoi/dot_config/nvim/lua/config/options.lua:12-19`:

```lua
if vim.env.SSH_CONNECTION or vim.env.SSH_TTY then
  local osc52 = require("vim.ui.clipboard.osc52")
  vim.g.clipboard = {
    name = "OSC 52",
    copy = { ["+"] = osc52.copy("+"), ["*"] = osc52.copy("*") },
    paste = { ["+"] = osc52.paste("+"), ["*"] = osc52.paste("*") },
  }
end
```

Note: OSC 52 is only forced when in an SSH session; locally it uses LazyVim's default provider (macOS `pbcopy`/`pbpaste`). For your shell command, the OSC-52 analog is emitting the escape sequence `\033]52;c;<base64-of-ref>\a` to the terminal (works locally and over SSH); a purely local shell command can just pipe to `pbcopy`.

## Exact rules to reproduce in a shell command

Reference string = `@` + `<path>` + `<suffix>`.

1. **Absolute path input:** the file's absolute path, no symlink resolution (shell: the path as given / `$PWD`-joined; do **not** `realpath` it for the `yF`/`ya` absolute flavors, to match `expand("%:p")`).
2. **Relative flavor (`yr`/`yf`):**
   - git root = `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` (this walks up for `.git` and is symlink-resolved, matching `LazyVim.root.git()`).
   - If the file is inside the root, path = file path relative to root, **no `./` prefix** (matches `vim.fs.relpath`).
   - Else fallback: path relative to cwd if under cwd; else `~/…` if under `$HOME`; else absolute (matches `:~:.`).
3. **Suffix:**
   - No line info (`yf`/`yF` equivalent) → empty.
   - Single line → `:N`.
   - Range → `:A-B` with `A <= B`; if `A == B`, collapse to `:A`.
4. **Prefix:** exactly one `@`, directly concatenated (e.g. `@lua/config/keymaps.lua:57-99`).
5. **Copy:** OSC 52 (`\033]52;c;$(printf %s "$ref" | base64)\a`) to match the Neovim SSH-safe behavior, or `pbcopy` for local-only.

Shapes produced: `@relpath`, `@relpath:12`, `@relpath:12-40`, and the absolute variants `@/abs/path`, `@/abs/path:12`, `@/abs/path:12-40`.



The relative path itself is computed by the built-in `vim.fs.relpath(root, abspath)` — it returns `abspath` expressed relative to `root` (e.g. `lua/config/keymaps.lua`), **with no leading `./`**, or `nil` if `abspath` is not inside `root`.

In a shell, `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` likewise returns a symlink-resolved path, so to match you should resolve the file path (or at least compare in the same symlink-space) before computing the relative segment — otherwise you'll hit the fallback more often than Neovim does.


When `LazyVim.root.git()` fails/returns nil, OR `vim.fs.relpath` returns nil (file not under root):

```lua

```

`:~:.` means: first make it relative to **cwd** if possible (`:.`), else make it relative to **home** with a `~` prefix (`:~`), else leave absolute. So a file under cwd → `subdir/file.txt`; a file under `$HOME` but outside cwd → `~/somewhere/file.txt`; otherwise the absolute path.

## `@` prefix and line suffix

- Prefix: literally `"@" .. path .. suffix` (`keymaps.lua:96`). Always a single leading `@`, no space.
- Suffix rules (`keymaps.lua:80-91`), only applied when `opts.lines` is set **and** `allow_line` is true (i.e. a real file buffer, not an explorer node):

```text
20	        "  PATH...   print each path's absolute form, one per line" \
21	        "  -r        resolve symlinks to the physical path (must exist)" \
22	        "  -t        abbreviate a \$HOME-rooted result to ~" \

61	
62	def abbrev(p):
```

**Should the `@file:line` copy-for-agent feature be a new dedicated shell command, or a flag bolted onto the existing `abspath`?**

Options:
- **New command (Recommended)** - A dedicated helper keeps `abspath` pipe-clean and single-purpose. It reuses `abspath` internally for the absolute path, but adds the `@` prefix, git-root-relative default, cwd flavor, and `:line` suffix. Gets its own row in aliases.md and clearer semantics.
- **Extend `abspath`** - Add e.g. `abspath --ref [--cwd] FILE:LINE` to the existing function. One entry point, but overloads abspath's documented 'pipe-clean absolute paths, like pwd' contract with `@`-prefix + git-relative + line-number behavior.

**If a new command, what should it be called? (Ignore if you chose 'Extend abspath'.)**

Options:
- **ref** - Shortest to type — 'copy a reference'. Minor conceptual overlap with git refs, but no shell-command collision in this repo.
- **cref** - 'copy ref' — mirrors the nvim `<leader>y`+`r` mnemonic and signals that it copies, not just prints.
- **atpath** - Evokes the `@` prefix and keeps the naming family with `abspath` / `tpath` in the same shell/ dir.
- **mention** - Descriptive: it builds a Claude/Cursor file-mention. Most self-explanatory, but the longest to type.

**By default, should the command copy to the clipboard, or just print like `abspath`?**

Options:
- **Copy to clipboard (Recommended)** - Pipe `@ref` through `x copy` (OSC 52, SSH-safe) and echo a `Copied @…` toast to stderr — matching the nvim feature's whole purpose and `tpath`'s house style. Still prints the ref to stdout so it stays pipeable. A `--no-copy`/`-n` flag opts out.
- **Print only** - Print `@ref` to stdout and leave copying to `| x copy`, exactly matching `abspath`'s pipe-clean contract. One extra step every time, but zero implicit clipboard writes.


**Answer:** New command (Recommended), cref, Copy to clipboard (Recommended)
</details></tool-use>
